candidate_c.token_boundary_hypothesis: Every actual citation block begins with '[' and accepted blocks are joined by exactly two LF characters. For the two exact registered tokenizer regexes, no pretokenizer alternative consumes the terminal LF and then '['. At the left segment's end, cl100k's end-of-string whitespace alternative consumes the same whole trailing whitespace as its newline alternative because the segment ends with LF. Therefore the sealed previous block plus separator and the next citation block are separate BPE pieces; their token-ID concatenation, and thus counts, are exact. This is a certified specific boundary, not arbitrary token-count additivity.
candidate_c.guard: Enable only with the exact known tokenizer version and inspected pattern hash, citation-prefix boundary and strict UTF-8 input certificate. Missing/unrecognized tokenizer internals, unsupported versions/patterns, non-citation headers or surrogate inputs retain the historical complete-context count and prefix-counter behavior, including historical errors.
candidate_c.reuse: Keep sealed-block counts only within one assembly call. Compute each previously accepted block plus separator once, then count only the new header/content. Supplemental stable-prefix checks may use the new header and the exactly sealed earlier-token total. No state or source/query text survives the call.
candidate_c.safe_fit_bound: For a certified strict-UTF-8 block, its UTF-8 byte length is an upper bound on its ordinary token count. If exact sealed-prefix tokens plus this bound fit, preserve that first-fit acceptance without an immediate encode. Final context_tokens must still be computed exactly; a later rejection cannot replace the accepted context or count.
